features.feature_value: Judged whether both comments together would contribute constructively to the conversation/topic.
features.evidence_span: evaluated whether or not both of the comments as a pair would contribute constructively
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes a pair-level constructive contribution criterion.

features.feature_value: Used whether the pair invited discussion vs being mostly insults/negative content.
features.evidence_span: whether or not they invited discussion or if they were just insults or negative content
features.rationale: They state a direct decision criterion focused on discussion invitation versus insults/negativity.

features.feature_value: Checked whether posts incited violence; if not, they were considered acceptable relative to sports cheering.
features.evidence_span: I looked to see if posts were inciting violence
features.rationale: They describe using violence incitement as a key gate for keep/remove decisions.

features.feature_value: Distinguished posts that seemed discussable from obvious rage bait.
features.evidence_span: actually something people could discuss vs obvious rage bait
features.rationale: They frame the influence as switching on whether content is meant for discussion or rage.

features.feature_value: Allowed posts with curse words as long as they were not threatening people; threats of violence would disallow.
features.evidence_span: clicked to allow them because they were not threatening people
features.rationale: They directly link cursing acceptance to absence of threats.

features.feature_value: Removed content that was aggressively rude if it added little to the subject matter; still endorsed free speech in general.
features.evidence_span: Anything too aggressively rude with logic I wanted removed because it did little to contribute
features.rationale: They describe a rule about rudeness and low contribution, plus a separate general preference for speech freedom.

features.feature_value: Weighted pros/cons and removed content when it contained radical misinformation; otherwise treated it as acceptable criticism.
features.evidence_span: radical information that indicated misinformation and was simply criticism that it was deemed ok
features.rationale: They explicitly separate misinformation from acceptable criticism as a decision driver.

features.feature_value: Noted posts closely matched left/right viewpoints; when cursing or perceived over-the-line content appeared, they thought both should not be used.
features.evidence_span: posts reflected very closely along the lines of what someone leaning left or right would say
features.rationale: They combine perceived partisan mirroring with a stricter threshold when cursing/out-of-line language occurs.
